text:
- [LDET.3.2.7] **Float canonical text form + Float→JSON serialization.** A finite
  `Float` renders as the **shortest decimal string that parses back to the
  identical IEEE-754 `double`** — the round-trip *shape*: fixed notation for
  `1e-4 ≤ |x| < 1e16`, scientific outside. In fixed notation the `.0` is
  **kept** on a whole float (`42.0` → `"42.0"`, never `"42"`, so the value
  round-trips as a `Float`, not collapsing to an `Int`). In scientific notation
  a mantissa of one digit carries no point (`1e16` → `"1e+16"`, never
  `"1.0e+16"`): the
  exponent already makes the text a `FLOAT_LIT` ([LLEX.11.2]). Lowercase signed
  exponent with ≥2 digits; `-0.0` preserved in
  the rendered text. A `Json` value holds no `-0.0` ([LGRA.5.8.8]), so none
  reaches its text. This shaping is DS-owned — it is *repr-shaped*, **not** Python-`repr`-identical: the runtime
  owns its own shaping and depends on no host `repr`. The compiler lowers a source
  `FloatLit` through the **same** shaping ([LUNI.2.7], [LUNI.17.7]), so a
  serialized cache value and the same value written as a source literal render
  alike, and a serialized cache value round-trips (`cached("k")` reads back what
  was written).

  **Determinism scope.** Both the shaping and the digits are the runtime's own,
  on every platform: the digits are correctly rounded and the form round-trips
  bit for bit ([LDET.3.2.8]). No host conversion routine takes part.

  **Non-finite on the JSON data plane — hard error.** The JSON data plane (the
  cache value, and every JSON value the engine builds) uses the finite form above; a **non-finite** `Float` (`±Inf`, or a
  NaN an expression produced, [LDET.3.6.2]) forced into a JSON
  body is a **`NOT_REPRESENTABLE` trap at the verb** ([LERR.1.4.9]): the engine
  abandons the activation and the verb does not run, so no `inf` token reaches
  the wire. A rule's path does not return `DS_ERR_JSON_NONFINITE`, which answers
  a host call that would build such a value ([LGRA.5.8.10]). A `Json`
  value holds none ([LGRA.5.8.10]), and no non-finite value is ever serialized
  to JSON.

  **±`Inf` text form (the text / display plane, not JSON).** Where a non-finite
  `Float` is rendered as **text** rather than JSON — `Float::String` ([LCST.4.5.6])
  and the display default below — `±Inf` renders `"inf"` / `"-inf"`. This clause is
  the home of both the finite canonical form and the `±Inf` text form; `[LCST.4.5.6]`
  references it.

  **Display default.** A string-interpolation segment with no
  explicit format spec (`"{x}"`), and `log` message text, render a `Float`
  in this **same** canonical form (faithful-by-default, the auto formatter); an
  explicit author format spec renders by [LGRA.2.9.6.5]'s rules. Display default, data plane
  and source-literal form are therefore one and the same shaping. *Carve-out:* the internal identity-value **row key** used for
  fact dedup is not observable rendering and is not governed here — `-0.0` is
  normalized to `0.0` in the identity / join float hashes ([LFAC.2]), and a
  `Float` used as an identity key already sits outside the cross-platform guarantee
  ([LDET.3.2.4] covers non-float slots).

idris.name: lcst_4_5_6__render_float
idris.note: The canonical text: `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`, `0.0` and `-0.0` each with its sign, and for a finite nonzero value the shortest digits in the clause's shape -- the double decomposed by exact halvings and doublings, `ldet_3_2_7__shortest`, the trailing zeros stripped, `ldet_3_2_7__shape`. Total but for a search that finds no digits, a trap no finite double reaches. The digits are found and checked by the model's own parse: run, not proved.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__after_point
idris.note: What follows the leading digit of a scientific mantissa: nothing when it is the only digit, else a point and the rest.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__and_right
idris.note: The right half of a true conjunction is true; a Bool lemma under the clause it serves.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__candidate_round_trips
idris.note: A candidate the search returns at one length passes `ldet_3_2_7__round_trips`: the choice admitted it with its own test true and by nothing else, for every value, length and candidate. What the test computes is run.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__candidates
idris.note: The two decimals of one length bracketing the value on that length's grid, each tested by the parse, the upper only when the value is not the lower exactly, the nearer and the parity of the lower handed to `ldet_3_2_7__choose`: a decimal of that length that parses back is one of the two, the decimals that parse back forming an interval around the value.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__candidates_by
idris.note: The choice at one length over an abstract test of a candidate: `lo` and `lo + 1` at power `p`, the two decimals of the length bracketing the value `lo + r / den`, each tested by `rt` (the upper only when the value is not `lo` exactly), the nearer and `lo`'s parity handed to `ldet_3_2_7__choose`. Abstract in the test so that `ldet_3_2_7__candidates_by_admit` is stated over variables and unfolds no parse; `ldet_3_2_7__candidates` is it at the parse's own test.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__candidates_by_admit
idris.note: A candidate the choice returns passed the test, whatever the test: `lo` with `rt lo p` true, or `lo + 1` with `rt (lo + 1) p` true, read off `ldet_3_2_7__chosen_was_admitted`. `ldet_3_2_7__candidate_round_trips` is this theorem at the parse's test.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__choose
idris.note: The clause's choice at one length as a case table and no `if`: the candidate that parses back; of two, the nearer; at an exact tie the even last digit ([LDET.3.2.8]'s rule); of none, nothing.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__chosen_was_admitted
idris.note: What the choice admits, read off its seven clauses: a chosen candidate is the lower with the lower parsing back, or the upper with the upper parsing back, at the power it was offered at, whatever the nearness and parity flags say.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__decimal_exponent
idris.note: The power of ten of a positive value's leading digit, from an estimate corrected a step at a time by exact comparison with powers of ten.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__fixed_form
idris.note: The clause's `1e-4 <= |x| < 1e16`, as the leading digit's power of ten from -4 to 15.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__found_round_trips
idris.note: The round trip by construction: whatever the search returns, at any length and from any starting length, passes `ldet_3_2_7__round_trips` for the value it was searched for -- the digits were admitted by the parse's own test. A theorem of the search's shape over every value; the test itself is run, not proved.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__ge_pow10
idris.note: Whether an exact fraction is at least a power of ten, for either sign of the exponent, by Integer comparison.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__just_inj
idris.note: `Just` is injective: the accepted duplicate of `lcyc_1_1__just_injective` in a module that imports none of the lane, base 0.8.0 having no `Injective Just`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__last_power
idris.note: The power of ten of the last of a given number of significant digits, from the leading digit's.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__round_trips
idris.note: The clause's 'parses back to the identical IEEE-754 double', read through the parse's own rounding: the decimal's nearest double (`ldet_3_2_8__nearest`), recomposed, is the value. What it computes is run against the fixtures and libds, not proved (the parse's proof is post-v1).

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__scaled10_den
idris.note: The divisor of an exact fraction scaled by a power of ten, with `ldet_3_2_7__scaled10_num` the numerator.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__scaled10_num
idris.note: The numerator of an exact fraction scaled by a power of ten of either sign.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__shape
idris.note: The shape: fixed notation from `1e-4` to below `1e16` with `.0` kept on a whole value and a `0` before a sub-one one, scientific outside it with a lowercase `e`, a signed exponent of at least two digits, a `-` first when negative, and no point after a one-digit scientific mantissa (`1e+16`, never `1.0e+16`), as the clause states; `ldet_3_2_7__shape_rows` executes `1e+16` and `1.5e+16`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__shape_rows
idris.note: Twelve rows of the shape on literal digits, each `Refl`: `42.0`, the fixtures' `0.30000000000000004` and `3.141592653589793`, the fixed form's edges `0.0001` and `9999999999999998.0`, the scientific `1e-05`, `1e+16`, `1.5e+16` and `-2.5e-07`, the extremes `5e-324` and `1.7976931348623157e+308`, `123456789.0`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__shortest
idris.note: The shortest digits of a finite nonzero magnitude by the clause's words -- among the decimals that parse back, the fewest significant digits; of that length the nearest; at a tie the even last digit -- searched from one digit upward. Partial on the bound: the search stops at seventeen digits, which the clause does not state; seventeen identify every binary64, so no finite value is left without digits, but that is a fact about the format and no theorem here, and a search that fails is a trap in `lcst_4_5_6__render_float`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__shortest_from
idris.note: The search from a length upward, a bounded number of lengths: the candidates at this length, else the next.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__shortest_step
idris.note: One step of the search: the candidates at this length when there are any, else the rest of the search, which arrives as a thunk so that a length that answers ends it.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__step_just
idris.note: A step that answers rests on the candidates at its length, or on the rest of the search with none at its length: the step's two clauses read back, over variables, for `ldet_3_2_7__found_round_trips`.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__strip
idris.note: The digits with their trailing zeros removed and the power of ten moved up by as many: one decimal, written with no trailing zero in the mantissa.

idris.name: ldet_3_2_7__two_digits
idris.note: The clause's exponent of at least two digits: a one-digit magnitude padded with a leading `0`.
